fields.v: Agent Skills (SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter + Markdown body + optional scripts/, references/, assets/), per the public Agent Skills specification supported by Anthropic (agentskills.io; version Not stated, accessed 28-06-2026); skills from the skills.sh registry and personal-use GitHub repositories

SKILL.md (frontmatter: name, description mandatory; license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools optional); optional scripts/, references/, assets/ directories; spec recommends body <= 500 lines, <= 5,000 whitespace tokens, relative Markdown links at most one directory deep. Content taxonomy found: scoping/orchestrating, execution lifecycle, output quality, governing agent conduct, domain knowledge, user/agent coordination

fields.v: SWEBOK KA distribution; reuse linkage and verbatim-copy rate (70.3% pairs similarity >= 0.99); upstream synchronisation (40.2% of never-updated reused skills missed upstream updates; 62.3% diverged); taxonomies of content (6 themes, 17 subthemes, 69 codes) and changes (6 themes, 60 codes); addition/removal ratio

Automatic mining (skills.sh, GitHub Search API, commit histories, LCS similarity); LLM classification (Qwen3.6-27b, temperature 0, validated against a 285-skill gold standard, kappa 0.82); manual thematic analysis and open coding by two authors; Mann-Whitney U, Cliff's delta, Fisher's exact with Benjamini-Hochberg, Cohen's h
N/A (document-based mining study; no configuration run)

Document-based: centralised (registry) vs personal-use skills on KA distribution, structure and specification conformance; customisation (registry-to-local adoption diff, 188 linked pairs) vs evolution (initial-to-final diff of locally authored skills, 256), stratified by similarity/churn quartiles. No agent, acceptance tests, repetitions or human intervention apply

Registry skills longer (median 1,678 vs 1,114 tokens; 19 vs 13 headers; p < 0.001, Cliff's delta 0.23/0.25) and more spec-conformant (name equals directory 97.65% vs 91.23%); optional fields in 3-16%. Reuse mostly one-time copy: 1,841/2,462 near-verbatim; 47.4% of reused skills locally updated vs 60.8% of local ones; 53% never updated after adoption. Most edited: reworking operational specifications (56.9% customisation / 61.6% evolution) and adapting knowledge (46.3% / 50.2%). Significant differences: repackaging/porting only in customisation (12.2% vs 0%, h = 0.71), renames/tool substitutions in evolution (5.3% vs 24.3%, h = 0.57), polishing presentation in customisation (55.9% vs 30.6%, h = 0.52). Additions outnumber removals 2.7:1 (evolution 6.1:1). User interaction, monitoring and failure-handling rules rarely edited

Distinguished registry vs personal and customisation vs evolution with statistical tests and effect sizes. Linkage heuristic validated (90% agreement, 93% genuine reuse in boundary bucket; 30/30 below threshold independent). Limitations stated: tests ignore clustering within repositories and dependence among labels; endpoint diff hides intermediate edits; exploratory

Single primary KA per skill; linkage misses renamed/heavily edited skills and assumes direction registry -> repo; customisation and evolution use different diff designs; 20-install threshold; LLM labels; gold standard stratified by predicted label; only public GitHub repos; Tukey cap may drop genuine projects; snapshot to March/May 2026; single registry. Gaps: consolidate re-authored domain knowledge, skill activation tracing, prose vs script trade-off, agent-neutral formats and templates

rev.why: Draft gave Yes. The only 'ground truth' is annotated by the authors themselves (gold standard, linkage audit, open coding), so it is not clearly independent of the authors' judgement; inter-rater agreement mitigates this. Yes or Partly both defensible.

The gold standard (kappa 0.85 between two annotators), the linkage audit and the thematic codes are all authored by the study's own authors (p. 4-5); the classifier is checked against that gold standard (kappa 0.82).
